proposal.comment: [Playbook] HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site and handles customer order data, but gives no indemnity. We have added a standard HDI defence and indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, unauthorised disclosure of Company data and wilful misconduct.

ops.text: Indemnification. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Site or any materials or technology provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) HDI's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Content, user information or customer data caused by HDI; or (iv) HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The Company shall give HDI prompt notice of the claim, and HDI shall control the defence and settlement with the Company's reasonable cooperation, provided that no settlement imposing any obligation on the Company shall be made without the Company's consent.

proposal.summary: Insert HDI indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and misconduct

quote: (b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement")
rationale: No indemnification, defence or hold-harmless language appears anywhere (a search for "indemn" returns nothing). HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and processes customer order data, so the absence of an IP-infringement indemnity is walk-away territory. We inserted the standard HDI indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice-and-control procedure; the Company gives no reciprocal indemnity, which we have left as is.
sectionRef: § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on ownership, so HDI would own the Site it builds and hosts and there is no licence back to us. We have confirmed that the Company owns its Content, the Site deliverables and all customer and user data, with HDI retaining its pre-existing tools and granting us a perpetual royalty-free licence to anything embedded in the Site.

ops.text: Ownership. As between the Parties, the Company owns all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Site (including all designs, code, text, images and other deliverables created for the Company under this Agreement, which HDI hereby assigns to the Company), the Marks, and all customer and user data collected through the Site. HDI retains ownership of its pre-existing and generally applicable tools, software and know-how, and grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any such HDI materials to the extent embedded in or necessary to operate the Site. No joint ownership is created by this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add ownership of Content, Site deliverables and customer data, with licence-back of HDI materials

quote: The Company shall have exclusive artistic and editorial control over the Site, including, without limitation, the implementation of the Content on the Site and the design and look and feel of the Site.
rationale: The Agreement never allocates ownership: HDI builds, hosts and bears all cost of the Site, so by default it would own the Site and its code with no licence back to us, and nothing states that the Company owns the Content or the customer/user order data HDI collects. Editorial control (5.2), merchant-of-record status (5.3) and the narrow Marks licence (6.1) do not cure this, and the Site access right in 1.4 dies with the term. We inserted an ownership provision confirming Company ownership of Content, Site deliverables and customer data, with HDI keeping its generic tools and granting a perpetual royalty-free licence.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
sectionRef: § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability at all, leaving both parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages. We have added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap.

ops.text: Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the amounts paid or payable by the Company to HDI under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) USD 1,000,000, and neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligation to pay amounts due under Section 3 shall not be treated as damages for purposes of this cap.

proposal.summary: Insert mutual liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs

rationale: There is no limitation of liability, damages exclusion or "aggregate liability" language anywhere in the Agreement — Section 9 contains only authority representations and Section 10 is boilerplate (the only uses of "liability" are the no-joint-venture disclaimers at 10.2). Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages. We have inserted a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
sectionRef: § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

quote: This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 10.3 imposes no consent requirement or prohibition on assignment and expressly runs to successors and assigns, so we may assign to an affiliate or an M&A successor freely — at least the fallback and, on its face, better. There is no change-of-control trigger and no HDI termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. Nothing to redline.
sectionRef: § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

quote: HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: The exclusivity granted to HDI sits at the fallback: it is confined to a defined product category (Deerskin Products on a self-contained Deerskin-branded site), runs only during a one-year term, carves out closeout merchandise (6.2), and we have performance-based exits (termination without penalty if the Site is not live within 70 days under 1.6, plus the notice-based non-renewal right in 4.1). Section 6.3 exclusivity runs in our favour. The residual breadth of the Company's restraint in the same sentence is redlined under NONCOMPETE rather than flagged twice here.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not pay liquidated damages; the Termination Payment formula (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is an uncapped penalty on us alone. We have capped it at three months' fees as the sole amount payable on termination.

ops.newText: the amount of which shall not exceed the aggregate amounts paid by the Company to HDI under Section 3.1 during the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date, which shall be the sole amount payable by the Company in respect of termination
ops.oldText: the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two

proposal.summary: Cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees

quote: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a one-way liquidated payment on the Company alone — 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, with no ceiling and payable even on a no-cause exit — while HDI owes nothing if it terminates (4.2(b)). That far exceeds the fallback of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. We capped it at three months' fees as the sole termination amount.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

ops.newText: the right to use (including by the Company's affiliates and by contractors acting on the Company's behalf, and by any successor to the Company), a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated

quote: the right to use, a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated, with a direct Internet connection of shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth, plus capacity to process continuously during burst periods.
rationale: The operative grant in Section 1.4 (system access plus HDI's software and Content administration tools) runs to the Company alone, with no coverage for affiliates or contractors acting on our behalf and no path to add them, which fails the fallback. It is at least not expressed as revocable at HDI's discretion, so this is not walk-away. We added affiliates, contractors and successors to the grant with a minimal edit.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we sell, and "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products ... and companies similar to" is open-ended. We have narrowed the covenant to a competing Deerskin-branded consumer web site during the term, with carve-outs for internal development and acquired businesses.

ops.newText: the Company shall not operate a self-contained web site offering Deerskin Products directly to consumers on the Internet (provided that this restriction shall not apply to the Company's internal development activities, to any business or product line acquired by the Company, or to any other products, brands or channels)
ops.oldText: the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)

proposal.summary: Narrow the restraint on the Company to the named Deerskin-branded site, with carve-outs

quote: during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
rationale: Section 6.1 restrains the Company (our side) from participating in "any project similar to the Site" for Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar" from "companies similar to" the named competitors — an open-ended field-of-use restriction that fails the fallback's requirement of a named competing product, and the only carve-out (6.2 closeout merchandise) does not cover internal development or acquisitions. It is term-only, so not walk-away, but we have narrowed it to a competing Deerskin-branded consumer site with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.

quote: unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other
rationale: Section 4.1 gives the Company a no-cause exit on 90 days' notice within an annual term, which sits at the fallback (60–90 days), and HDI's mirror right is also at 90 days rather than the sub-90-day notice that would be walk-away; Section 1.6 adds a penalty-free exit if the Site is not live in 70 days. The uncapped Termination Payment in Section 4.2 is the real problem and is redlined once, under LD, rather than flagged twice; our RENEWAL redline also shortens our own notice to 30 days while leaving HDI at 90.

quote: HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours.
rationale: Section 3.4 already meets our position on notice (30 days), business hours, scope (payment-calculation records only), cost (HDI bears it) and no system access, but there is no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly — the fallback requires once per year. We added a once-per-twelve-months cap with a single minimal edit; the absence of an independent-auditor requirement is noted but not flagged.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
rationale: New York law is our preferred governing law and there is no arbitration clause or foreign venue. The clause is silent on forum (no express submission to the New York courts), which we note as a minor gap rather than a deviation.

rationale: The only "no less favorably" undertaking runs in our favour — HDI must promote the Site and Deerskin Products at least as favourably as its own catalog titles, at HDI's cost. There is no obligation on the Company to extend HDI terms matching those given to third parties, so nothing to redline.

quote: The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month.
rationale: Fees are purely a revenue share on actual Net Sales, with the first $11,000 per month excluded; there is no minimum spend, guaranteed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic anywhere (no hits for "minimum"), and no volume cap on our usage. This matches our preferred position. The separate Termination Payment is addressed under LD.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 90-day non-renewal window is longer than we accept on an annually auto-renewing term; we have moved the Company to 30 days while leaving HDI at 90 days so it cannot exit on short notice.

ops.newText: unless terminated by the Company upon thirty (30) days written notice to HDI, or by HDI upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company
ops.oldText: unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other

proposal.summary: Shorten the Company's non-renewal notice window to 30 days, keep HDI at 90 days

quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
rationale: The Agreement auto-renews annually with a 90-day non-renewal notice window, which exceeds the fallback of no more than 60 days. The 12-month renewal length is acceptable and there is no renewal price uplift (fees are a revenue share), so no uplift cap is needed. We shortened the Company's window to 30 days while leaving HDI at 90 days so HDI cannot exit on shorter notice; absence of a renewal reminder is noted but not flagged.
sectionRef: § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The termination article says nothing about getting our Content and customer data back or migrating the Site. We have added six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of data in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at HDI's then-current rates, including cooperation in migrating the Site to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to the Company all Content, user information and customer and order data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion obligations

rationale: Article 4 deals only with term, notice and the Termination Payment; nothing requires HDI to hand back our Content, user information or customer/order data, to assist with migrating the Site, or to delete data afterwards, and the Section 1.4 access rights do not survive (10.7 preserves only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10). We inserted a transition-assistance and data-return provision as new Section 4.3 (six months' assistance at HDI's rates, return within 30 days, certified deletion).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

ops.text: HDI warrants that (1) the design, development, hosting, operation, maintenance and management of the Site will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards and in compliance with applicable law; (2) for a period of ninety (90) days following the Effective Date, the Site will conform in all material respects to the specifications approved by the Company under Section 5.2; and (3) the Site will not contain any virus or other malicious code. The Company's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at HDI's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the amounts paid by the Company in respect of the non-conforming services.

proposal.summary: Insert performance and conformance warranty with a remedy

quote: Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation;
rationale: Section 9 contains only mutual corporate-authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement — there is no warranty that HDI's development, hosting and operation of the Site will be performed competently, that the Site will conform to the specifications we approve, or any remedy. The launch deadline in 1.6 is a delivery milestone, not a performance warranty. We inserted a workmanlike/conformance/no-malicious-code warranty with a re-performance, repair or refund remedy; there is no disclaimer to carve out.

ops.text: Insurance. HDI shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where HDI processes Content, user information or customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. rationale: There is no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement (a search for "insur" returns nothing).
